title: Inflight toolname hints and stream-safe rewrite
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: During token-by-token streaming the assistant may emit partial hints (e.g., 'call the weath' then 'er.getForecast') or ambiguous identifiers that map to multiple legacy functions. Current name-resolution runs post-hoc and/or blocks streaming until the full name is present, which either breaks live UX (stalling) or causes incorrect mapping. We need a runtime shim that can: 1) extract in-flight name hints from the token stream, 2) propose canonical mappings with confidence scores, 3) perform stream-safe rewrites or graceful fallbacks to legacy function signatures, and 4) preserve streaming semantics (no dropping of tokens, proper tool-call boundaries, idempotency of calls).
acceptance_criteria: Token-level streaming remains uninterrupted for 95% of test prompts that include tool calls (no >200ms added tail latency due to name resolution).

When the stitcher proposes a mapping with confidence >= 0.85, runtime emits a tool-call event that matches the legacy function contract and the downstream function is invoked successfully in canary tests.

When confidence < 0.85, the system waits up to a 300ms grace window for additional tokens, then either selects a best-effort fallback or inserts a standardized 'unknown-tool' telemetry event (no silent drop).
All tool invocations originating from streaming paths are logged with provenance (original tokens, resolved name, confidence) and viewable in Console telemetry for debugging.
Feature gated behind flag 'stream_inflight_name_hints' with gradual rollout to 10%, 50%, 100% traffic and automatic rollback on error rate increase >3x baseline.
Automated integration tests that simulate partial-token emissions and ambiguous alias sets pass in CI and on dedicated canary nodes.
proposed_solution: Create a lightweight 'inflight-stitcher' component inside the invocation broker that consumes assistant token events in real-time and maintains a sliding name-hint buffer (max 128 chars).
Implement a small probabilistic matcher backed by the canonical name registry and lemmatized token fuzzy matching (edit distance + token subsequence heuristics).

Expose two decision paths: 'auto-resolve' (confidence >= threshold) which emits an immediate tool-call envelope, and 'defer-and-collect' which delays up to a short grace window for more tokens before deciding.
For auto-resolve path, write a stream-aware marshaller that synthesizes the legacy function payload while streaming remaining tokens to the client (no token duplication).
Add a 'stitch-proof' header in the runtime protocol to mark events mutated by the stitcher for audit and downstream idempotency guards.
Instrument telemetry: resolution_confidence, resolution_latency, fallback_reason, and duplicate_invoke_guard metrics. Surface these in Console under per-route tool-call diagnostics.
Feature flag gating and a canary rollout plan; unit tests and a dedicated end-to-end suite that replays recorded streaming transcripts from customer traces (sanitized).
implementation_notes: Runtime changes required in invocation-broker and stream-marshaller layers; keep the stitcher as a small, well-instrumented hot path to minimize overhead.
Add canonical-name cache with TTL and invalidation hooks tied to the alias registry change stream (to prevent stale mappings).
Memory/CPU: stitcher runs per-connection but holds only a small ring buffer; expected additional CPU < 2% on canary GPUs for typical workloads.
API/contract: no public API changes. Internal tool-call event structure adds optional 'resolved_from_hint' and 'resolution_confidence' fields (backwards-compatible).
Testing: generate fuzz transcripts (obfuscated real traces) that include partial token splits, hyphenation, escaped characters, and non-ASCII identifiers to validate matcher robustness.
risks_and_mitigation: Increased latency: mitigate by keeping decision threshold conservative and using short grace windows; measure and iterate.

Wrong mapping => incorrect function invoked: mitigate via confidence threshold, immediate telemetry, and automatic circuit-breaker that pauses auto-resolve after 5 false positives per minute per route.
Duplicate invocation risk when speculative resolve and later explicit tool call both occur: add idempotency token derived from streaming session and resolved span to suppress duplicates downstream.

Security: tool args may contain secrets if stitched incorrectly; ensure the stitcher never emits expanded args without passing them through the same KMS/Audit path as normal tool calls and add a sanitizer that strips obvious PII before telemetry export.
Operational complexity: mitigate via clear runbook, a single feature flag, and runbooks for rolling back should error rates increase.
comments: 2025-03-19 - Design sync w/ PM (Owen Martinez) and Runtime (Rajat): agreed to prioritize no-regressions on streaming UX. Decided on 300ms grace window as starting point.
2025-03-21 - Prototype landed in branch feature/inflight-stitcher. Simple matcher implemented using trigram subsequence scoring. Initial canary showed +40ms median on synthetic traces.
2025-03-25 - Telemetry schema PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3726. Added fields: resolved_from_hint (bool), resolution_confidence (float), resolution_path (enum).
2025-03-28 - Privacy review: asked Legal to sign off on sanitized trace export. Legal (Sofia Alvarez) requested explicit opt-in for customer-supplied trace replay. Marked as security_review_required.

2025-04-01 - Stress run on canary nodes: observed 0.9% increase in error rate for routes with heavy legacy function traffic; rolled feature to 5% and enabled circuit-breaker tuning. Investigating root cause (likely malformed payload edge-case).

2025-04-02 - Action items: (1) add idempotency token generation before emitting auto-resolved call, (2) tighten matcher to prefer full-token boundaries, (3) add more negative testcases for edge unicode names. Rajat assigned to implement fixes.
